title: Helicity-Controlled Hall Transport in Hybrid Topological Magnetic Textures
authors: Anton V. Hlushchenko, Julia Kharlan, Mykhailo I. Bratchenko, Aleksei V. Chechkin, Jarosław W. Kłos, Oleg A. Tretiakov
abstract: Topological magnetic textures can serve as information carriers driven by spin currents. However, their motion is generally accompanied by a Hall effect that deflects them from the current direction, limiting transport efficiency and controllability. We develop a unified spin-space transformation framework enabling a systematic study of hybrid spin textures with different helicities, such as skyrmions, antiskyrmions, bimerons, and antibimerons. Combining analytical theory with micromagnetic simulations, we establish the relation between helicity and current-driven transport. An analytical solution of the generalized Thiele equation identifies helicity as a geometric control parameter and yields a simple expression for the Hall angle, enabling its continuous tuning, complete suppression, and deterministic steering along arbitrary in-plane directions. Micromagnetic simulations confirm that the generated spin textures remain stable under Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert dynamics and validate the analytical predictions. These results establish helicity as a versatile control parameter for programmable transport of topological magnetic textures.
summary: This work introduces a unified theoretical framework to study hybrid topological magnetic textures, treating helicity as a key geometric control parameter. By analyzing the dynamics using the generalized Thiele equation, the authors demonstrate that helicity can deterministically tune the Hall angle, thereby enabling programmable and highly controllable spin-current transport. The results are validated through comparison with micromagnetic simulations.
main_problem: The primary goal is to overcome the inherent Hall effect that limits the efficiency and controllability of transporting topological magnetic textures driven by spin currents.
main_result: The study establishes helicity ($\eta$) as a versatile geometric control parameter, allowing for the deterministic tuning, complete suppression, or precise steering of the Hall angle during texture transport.
method: The authors combine analytical theory, utilizing a generalized Thiele equation derived from a unified spin-space transformation framework, with micromagnetic simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves hybrid topological magnetic textures (skyrmions, bimerons, etc.) whose dynamics are governed by micromagnetic energy functionals incorporating exchange, anisotropy, and Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI).
key_observables: Hall angle ($	heta_H$), longitudinal and transverse velocities ($v_x, v_y$), and the dependence of transport on helicity ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Helicity ($\eta$), topological charge ($Q$), and the material parameters governing the DMI and anisotropy.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the rigid-body approximation for dynamics and, in some derivations, an isotropic approximation for the dissipative tensor.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spin-space transformation framework generating various hybrid textures, and show the dependence of velocity components on helicity, comparing analytical Thiele equation predictions with micromagnetic simulation results.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops a unified spin-space transformation framework to construct multiple families of topological textures. It then applies this framework to derive analytical expressions for the dynamics via the generalized Thiele equation, demonstrating how helicity controls the Hall angle, which is subsequently validated by micromagnetic simulations.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the concept of using a geometric parameter (helicity) to control a transport response (Hall angle) via an equation of motion (Thiele equation) is analogous to controlling quantum system responses using geometric phases or topological invariants.
